answer: A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The wharf multiplier is published, charged in terrace, and mirror lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 20 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 3986 identities would post 3686 proofs and burn roughly 56 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
